_comment: The canonical claim is a real invoice in a real accounting system, read back through an
authenticated call. Variants are the SAME claim rewritten the way a second lender would
receive it, so k-of-N matching has something to measure; the last entry is a different
claim and must NOT match, which is what keeps the threshold from being tuned to accept
everything. Every canonical value below was returned by the provider, none was invented.
The tax id carries its separators as the source system stores them, so the reformatting
runs in the direction the real data dictates: canonical has spaces, the variant strips them.

variants.label: amount written with a decimal separator
